title: Choose the landing page's structure
question: Three structures for pg_auth's landing page, in the pg_auth look (dark ink, Supabase green, code on screen). The roll put the policy-diff first. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: The policy file collapses
options.thesis: The first screen is a diff: a Supabase-style RLS file (helper functions, four policies) struck through, replaced by one authz.protect line, with the model and a grant-by-row beside it.
options.viewport: Headline and two actions (boot the demo, read the guide) on the left; the diff and two small cards (the model, a grant written as a row) on the right. The live demo follows directly below.
options.risk: Leads with what you stop writing, so it compares to RLS on the first screen; must stay about effort, never speed.

options.label: The demo is the first screen
options.thesis: Postgres, the sidecar and OpenFGA boot in the tab: a step rail on the left (protect, grant as a row, Bob sees, why, revoke), Anne's and Bob's psql side by side, the sidecar's log underneath showing the delivery.
options.viewport: A compact headline, then the multi-window demo fills the viewport; the boot button is the primary action.
options.risk: Before boot, the first screen is a poster of terminals; the headline has to carry the offer on its own.

options.label: One app, three acts, the demo beside you
options.thesis: A narrated walk through one app (a team document editor): Act I protect, Act II grant by inserting a row, Act III ask why. The demo stays pinned on the right and follows the act you are reading.
options.viewport: Headline and the three acts as a timeline on the left; the demo frame with tabs (admin, anne, bob, sidecar) on the right, Act I typed in.
options.risk: Scroll-linked, so it needs careful fallback on phones and with reduced motion.
